en: Petrol prices go up almost every month.
tamil: பெட்ரோல் விலை கிட்டத்தட்ட ஒவ்வொரு மாசமும் ஏறுது.
context: Complaining about fuel cost with a colleague.
explain: Simple present with 'almost every month' shows a regular pattern.
usage: Use it in casual talk when people discuss rising costs.
leelaQ: How do rising petrol prices affect your life?
answer: I now use public transport more often.

en: Is there any charge for withdrawing cash?
tamil: பணம் எடுக்க ஏதாவது கட்டணம் இருக்கா?
context: Asking at the bank about ATM fees.
explain: 'Is there any ...?' checks whether something exists.
usage: Ask it at the bank or ATM counter before taking out money.
leelaQ: Do you carry cash or do you mostly use your phone?
answer: I carry a little cash and use my phone for the rest.

en: I am waiting for the SMS from the bank.
tamil: வங்கியில இருந்து SMS-காக காத்துட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling someone why you cannot finish a payment.
explain: 'Am waiting for' shows you are in the middle of waiting.
usage: Use it when an OTP or confirmation has not come yet.
leelaQ: What do you do when an OTP does not arrive?
answer: I wait for one minute and then ask for it again.

en: Could you help me fill this deposit slip?
tamil: இந்த டெபாசிட் சீட்டை நிரப்ப உதவ முடியுமா?
context: Asking a bank staff member for help.
explain: 'Could you help me ...?' is polite when you need support.
usage: Use it with bank staff or a helpful person when a form is confusing.
leelaQ: Who helps you when you do not understand a form?
answer: My brother helps me with forms.

en: I will pay you back by next Monday.
tamil: அடுத்த திங்கள்கிழமைக்குள்ள உங்களுக்கு திருப்பி கொடுத்துடறேன்.
context: Promising a friend to return borrowed money.
explain: 'Pay back' means return money. 'By' gives a deadline.
usage: Say it when you borrow a small amount from a friend or relative.
leelaQ: Is it a good idea to borrow money from friends?
answer: It is fine for small amounts if we pay back on time.

en: I never lend money to strangers.
tamil: தெரியாதவங்களுக்கு நான் ஒருநாளும் பணம் கடன் கொடுக்கமாட்டேன்.
context: Explaining your rule about money.
explain: 'Never' makes the sentence negative. It is used with habits.
usage: Use it to politely refuse when an unknown person asks for money.
leelaQ: Would you lend money to a close friend?
answer: Yes, I would lend a small amount to a close friend.

en: I got a message about a failed transaction.
tamil: தோல்வியடைந்த பரிவர்த்தனை பத்தி ஒரு மெசேஜ் வந்தது.
context: Telling the bank about a payment problem.
explain: 'Got a message' is a common spoken way to say 'received a message'.
usage: Use it on a bank helpline call when money is cut but not received.
leelaQ: What will you do if money is cut but the payment fails?
answer: I will call the bank and give the transaction details.

en: Have you paid the house rent this month?
tamil: இந்த மாசம் வீட்டு வாடகை கட்டிட்டீங்களா?
context: Asking your flatmate about rent.
explain: 'Have you ...?' asks whether something is done by now.
usage: Ask it to a flatmate or family member who handles the rent.
leelaQ: Who pays the rent in your home?
answer: My father pays the rent every month.

en: Gold rate is high these days.
tamil: இப்போ தங்கம் விலை ரொம்ப அதிகமா இருக்கு.
context: Chatting with relatives before a wedding.
explain: 'These days' means at the present time.
usage: Use it in family talk about jewellery or weddings.
leelaQ: Do people in your family buy gold for weddings?
answer: Yes, we always buy some gold for weddings.

en: Tell me the exact amount before you swipe the card.
tamil: கார்டை தேய்க்கறதுக்கு முன்னாடி சரியான தொகையை சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking a cashier to confirm the bill.
explain: 'Before' connects two actions in order. 'Exact' means correct, not roughly.
usage: Say it at a shop counter so you can check the total.
leelaQ: Why should we check the amount before we pay?
answer: So we do not pay a wrong amount by mistake.

en: We can save more if we cook at home.
tamil: வீட்டுல சமைச்சா நிறைய சேமிக்கலாம்.
context: Talking about reducing food expenses.
explain: 'If' sentences show a condition and its result.
usage: Use it when you discuss ways to spend less with family.
leelaQ: What is one habit that helps you save money?
answer: I carry lunch from home to save money.

en: Do you accept Google Pay here?
tamil: இங்க Google Pay வாங்கிப்பீங்களா?
context: Asking a shopkeeper before buying.
explain: 'Do you accept ...?' asks which payment ways a shop allows.
usage: Ask it at a small shop or restaurant before you order.
leelaQ: Which payment method do you use the most?
answer: I use UPI the most.

en: My card has expired, so I need a new one.
tamil: என் கார்டு காலாவதி ஆகிடுச்சு, அதனால புது கார்டு வேணும்.
context: Talking to bank staff about a card problem.
explain: 'So' connects a reason with a result.
usage: Use it at the bank counter or on a helpline when you need a replacement.
leelaQ: What do you do when your bank card stops working?
answer: I visit the bank and ask for a new card.

en: I did not receive the refund yet.
tamil: ரீஃபண்ட் இன்னும் எனக்கு வரல.
context: Calling customer care about a refund.
explain: 'Did not receive' is the negative past. 'Yet' shows you still expect it.
usage: Say it to customer care when an online order refund is late.
leelaQ: How long do you wait for a refund before you complain?
answer: I wait for about a week and then I call them.

en: The shopkeeper gave me ten rupees extra change by mistake.
tamil: கடைக்காரர் தவறுதலா எனக்கு பத்து ரூபாய் அதிகமா சில்லறை கொடுத்துட்டார்.
context: Telling a friend about an honest moment.
explain: 'By mistake' means not on purpose.
usage: Use it when you tell a story about money and honesty.
leelaQ: What would you do if a shopkeeper gave you extra change?
answer: I would return the extra money to him.

en: Could I pay half now and half later?
tamil: பாதி இப்போ, பாதி அப்புறம் கட்டலாமா?
context: Asking a shop owner for a payment option.
explain: 'Could I ...?' is a polite way to ask for something unusual.
usage: Ask it when you need to split a payment with a shop or a school office.
leelaQ: Do you like to pay in parts or all at once?
answer: I like to pay all at once, so I am free of tension.

en: Prices will come down after the festival season.
tamil: பண்டிகை சீசன் முடிஞ்சதும் விலை குறையும்.
context: Advising a friend to wait before buying.
explain: 'Will' is used for a prediction. 'Come down' means become lower.
usage: Use it when you tell someone to wait for a better price.
leelaQ: When do you usually shop for clothes or gadgets?
answer: I shop during big festival sales.

en: He is checking the bill line by line.
tamil: அவர் பில்லை ஒவ்வொரு வரியா சரிபார்க்கிறார்.
context: Describing a careful person at a restaurant.
explain: 'Line by line' means slowly, one line at a time.
usage: Use it when you describe someone who is very careful with money.
leelaQ: Do you check your bill carefully at restaurants?
answer: Yes, I always check it before I pay.

en: Would you mind splitting the bill with me?
tamil: பில்லை என்கூட பிரிச்சுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend to share the cost.
explain: 'Would you mind ...ing?' is a gentle and polite request.
usage: Use it after a meal when friends share the cost.
leelaQ: Do you share bills with friends when you eat out?
answer: Yes, we split the bill equally.

en: I opened a recurring deposit last week.
tamil: போன வாரம் ஒரு ஆர்.டி. கணக்கு தொடங்கினேன்.
context: Telling a colleague about a savings plan.
explain: 'Opened' is the past of 'open'. A recurring deposit means saving a fixed amount monthly.
usage: Use it when you talk about savings plans with colleagues.
leelaQ: What is a good way to save a little money every month?
answer: A recurring deposit is a good way to save every month.

en: What is the minimum balance in this account?
tamil: இந்த கணக்குல குறைந்தபட்ச இருப்பு எவ்வளவு?
context: Asking the bank before opening an account.
explain: 'Minimum balance' is the least money you must keep in the account.
usage: Ask it at the bank before you open any new account.
leelaQ: Why is it important to know the minimum balance?
answer: Because the bank can charge a fee if we go below it.

en: I keep a small emergency fund for sudden expenses.
tamil: திடீர் செலவுகளுக்கு கொஞ்சம் அவசர நிதி வச்சிருக்கேன்.
context: Explaining your saving habit.
explain: 'Keep' is used for money you set aside. 'Sudden' means unexpected.
usage: Use it when you talk about safe money habits with friends.
leelaQ: What kind of sudden expenses can happen in a family?
answer: A medical bill or a repair can happen suddenly.

en: You cannot withdraw more than ten thousand rupees from this ATM.
tamil: இந்த ATM-ல பத்தாயிரத்துக்கு மேல எடுக்க முடியாது.
context: Explaining the daily limit to a friend.
explain: 'Cannot' shows a limit or rule. 'More than' compares amounts.
usage: Use it to warn someone about an ATM limit.
leelaQ: How much cash do you usually take out at one time?
answer: I take out about two thousand rupees at one time.

en: The EMI is deducted from my account on the fifth.
tamil: EMI ஐந்தாம் தேதி என் கணக்குல இருந்து பிடிச்சுக்குவாங்க.
context: Explaining a monthly loan payment.
explain: Passive 'is deducted' focuses on what happens to the money.
usage: Use it when you tell someone why you need money in the account by a date.
leelaQ: Which date of the month is hardest for you money-wise?
answer: The end of the month is hardest because my money is finished.

en: I'm going to start a small SIP next month.
tamil: அடுத்த மாசம் ஒரு சின்ன SIP தொடங்கப் போறேன்.
context: Telling a friend about investing.
explain: 'I'm going to' shows a plan. A SIP is a monthly investment.
usage: Use it when you talk about your investment plan with friends.
leelaQ: What would you like to invest in some day?
answer: I would like to invest in mutual funds.
